title: 3 Invisible Excel Problems That Break XLOOKUP & Power Query
description:
Your Excel data can look perfectly clean and still fail. This tutorial demonstrates three invisible problems that cause real lookup and Power Query errors: nonbreaking spaces that TRIM alone does not remove, ambiguous date parsing caused by locale/culture, and Remove Duplicates preserving an unexpected row after sorting. You’ll see each failure happen in a realistic worksheet or Power Query editor, diagnose the cause, apply the fix, and verify the result.

#excel #powerquery #xlookup #datacleaning #automation

rules: real Excel/Power Query UI remains dominant
purposeful animation only when explaining invisible state
visible cursor and click targets when teaching steps
small lower captions; no giant centered subtitle wall
include one thumbnail-candidate frame inside the video because custom thumbnail may be unavailable
signature_moments: x-ray sweep reveals U+00A0 hidden space
calendar morph shows one date string becoming two different dates under different cultures

scenes.title: Cold open — looks clean, still broken
scenes.narration: Three datasets look normal. One lookup fails, one date changes meaning, and one duplicate cleanup keeps the wrong record. The problem is not what you can see.

scenes.title: Bug 1 — hidden nonbreaking space
scenes.narration: TRIM removes normal ASCII spaces, but Microsoft documents that it does not remove the nonbreaking space character with decimal value 160. Diagnose it with length and character-code checks, then replace CHAR(160) before trimming.

scenes.title: Fix 1 — clean and verify XLOOKUP
scenes.narration: Use a replacement-plus-TRIM cleanup, rerun the lookup, and compare the cleaned identifier against the original so the fix is proven rather than assumed.

scenes.title: Bug 2 — dates depend on locale
scenes.narration: Power Query culture controls how text dates are interpreted. The same slash-formatted text can produce different meanings under different regional settings.

scenes.title: Fix 2 — parse with an explicit culture or format
scenes.narration: Set the intended regional culture or use an explicit parsing format, then verify the converted date against a known source value.

scenes.title: Bug 3 — Remove Duplicates keeps an unexpected row
scenes.narration: Microsoft documents that Table.Distinct does not guarantee which duplicate will be preserved because query folding and optimization can change evaluation.

scenes.title: Fix 3 — buffer the sorted table before distinct
scenes.narration: Sort by the business rule, buffer the table, then remove duplicates. Verify the survivor is the intended latest record.

scenes.title: Final checklist
scenes.narration: When Excel data looks correct but behaves wrong, test invisible characters, culture, and evaluation order before blaming the formula.
